Can those two credits be "stacked" against the same usage (i.e., apply stipend + sandbox credit to reduce the same invoice period), or do they need to be treated separately?

Two follow-ups we care about: 1) How will this show up on the invoice / can you provide a sample invoice line item? 2) Are there any procurement tax/treatment implications we should prepare for (credit notes vs invoice adjustments)?

Hi Aisha — thanks for sending this over and congrats on the stipend. Short answer: we can make the economics work either as stacked credits or as a credit note flow, but there are accounting and operational trade-offs; below are two pragmatic options and the implications so your finance team can pick.

Option A — Voucher stacking (preferred for startups):
- We apply the sandbox credit first to usage.
- Sponsor stipend is issued as a separate voucher that can be redeemed against subsequent invoices until exhausted.
- Outcome on invoice: usage reduced by sandbox credit; stipend appears as a separate line-item voucher (non-taxable credit note for most customers).
- Pros: keeps invoice semantics simple, faster to implement.
- Cons: both credits cannot reduce a single invoice line (we can’t double-count the same usage token).

Option B — Consolidated accounting adjustment (consolidation):
- We apply stipend as an immediate credit note against the same invoice period and post an adjusted invoice showing net zero / net usage.
- Requires coordination with our billing/finance team to issue an adjusted invoice and credit note tied to your PO.
- Pros: single net invoice, easier for some procurement teams.
- Cons: requires an additional billing workflow and manual reconciliation on both sides.

Next steps I recommend: 1) If you prefer Voucher stacking, confirm and we’ll provision stipend as a redeemable voucher and send sample invoice lines; 2) If you prefer Consolidation, loop in your AP contact and any PO numbers so Mina can draft the credit note path.

I’m attaching a quick mutual action plan (MAP) so we can reflect whichever path you choose and map owners / timelines.

Jordan

Hi Aisha — Mina from Finance here. Quick accounting/ops clarifications so your procurement team can decide: 

1) We cannot apply two separate credits to reduce the exact same invoice line items in our automated billing system (it would effectively double-count).

2) To accomplish a "net zero" effect on the same billing period we issue a credit note (manual adjustment) referencing the invoice number. That is Option B above. The credit note will appear as a separate document and reduce the net amount owed for that period.

3) If you accept the stipend as a redeemable voucher (Option A), it will be issued as a voucher code tied to your account and will show up as a line item "Voucher redemption" on future invoices when applied. This is easier operationally and faster to reconcile for cohort startups.

4) Tax/procurement: credit notes are typically non-taxable adjustments in most states but procurement teams sometimes prefer an adjusted invoice + credit for audit trails. If Foundry needs an adjusted invoice for audit, please provide: billing contact, PO number, and the invoice(s) you want adjusted.

5) If you need a temporary top-up while we finalize the credit routing (e.g., runway protection for startups), we can provision a short-term emergency voucher (30 days) but this requires manager approval — Jordan / Marissa, can we approve an emergency +30d voucher for Foundry cohort startups?

Sending a template for the credit note for your AP team to review.

Thanks,
